# Aeris-M Field Safety Datasheet

Applies to: all Aeris-M soil-moisture probes, Revision 1 and Revision 2. Issued by Kellerman Instruments, 2031-02-01.

## 1. Hazard summary

Each Aeris-M probe contains one factory-sealed lithium thionyl chloride primary cell. Lithium thionyl chloride cells can vent violently if overheated, crushed, punctured, or discharged incorrectly. Treat every unit as energized at all times.

## 2. Storage

- Store below 60 C. Storage above 60 C may cause cell venting.
- Store in dry, ventilated areas away from flammable material.
- Do not stack more than six transport cases high.

## 3. Prohibited handling

- Never incinerate, crush, puncture, or attempt to disassemble an Aeris-M unit in the field.
- Never attempt to replace or recharge the cell; the housing is welded shut.
- Never ship a damaged unit by air freight.

## 4. Exposure response

If an electrolyte odour is detected near a probe, evacuate and ventilate the enclosure before approaching the unit. Do not touch a vented cell with bare hands. Summon the site safety officer and record the event in the site register before resuming work.

## 5. Return and disposal

- Recovered units must be returned to Kellerman Instruments for cell removal.
- Disposal in general waste is prohibited.
- The return consignment form is DSV-44; damaged units travel under UN3090 labeling.

## 6. Field transport

Probes travel in the factory shock sleeve with the cell terminals shielded. A probe dropped more than two meters must be quarantined and inspected before redeployment, even when no visible damage is present.

## 7. Temperature limits reminder

The probe operates from -20 C to +60 C, but operation near either limit reduces measurement stability. The storage ceiling of 60 C is an absolute limit and is lower than the +70 C operating ceiling of some competitor products; do not transfer handling rules between product lines.
